answer: A port-authority model: every agent must dock at a public jetty where its past work is kept as a verifiable relic — a signed, timestamped log of completed jobs and payments. New identities start with no relic and may only take tiny, escrowed tasks. A beacon service publishes this reputation ledger so any counterparty can check an agent's history before trusting it. Faking one identity is cheap, but faking a deep, attested work history costs real time and real completed jobs, so a flood of fresh sybil accounts is easy to spot and cheap to ignore.
